newsitem.title: USA: Levi Strauss says 1996 sales top $7.1 billion.
newsitem.headline: Levi Strauss says 1996 sales top $7.1 billion.

text.p: Levi Strauss & Co. said Wednesday its worldwide sales of jeans and other clothing rose 6 percent to $7.1 billion last year, a record for the world's largest apparel manufacturer.
In the United States, sales topped $4.3 billion, driven by demand for the Levi's and Dockers brands, the privately held company said in a statement.
Sales of its new line of men's dress pants, called Slates, "grew at a pace exceeding company expectations," it said.
International sales were $2.8 billion, led by demand in Germany and Britiain.
A strong European performance was offset by "slightly lower sales" in the Asia-Pacific region. Levi cited sluggish economies in Japan, South Korea and Australia as hurting sales in Asia.
